points.text: During the last stage of Prophet (s.a.w.s)’s residence at Makkah, the message of Islam had reached different parts of Arabia and especially to Madinah. The Jews in Madinah wanted to test Muhammad (s.a.w.s) and they instigated the unbelievers to ask the Prophet: “Why did the Israelites go to Egypt?”. The Israelites are the children of Yaqoob (a.s) who is the son of Ishaaq (a.s) and grandson of Ibraheem (a.s).

It was a known fact that Ibrahim (a.s) was from Palestine and Yaqoob (a.s) was also born and raised in Palestine. During the time of Musa, Musa had taken the Israelites out from Egypt and away from the clutches of Firaun. But the question was, how did the Israelites come to Egypt in the first place. The history of Israelites was not known to the Arabs. So the Jews thought that the Prophet (s.a.w.s) would not be able to give a satisfactory answer. Allah revealed Surah Yousuf and the Prophet (s.a.w.s) recited the whole story then and there, thereby ruining the schemes of the unbelievers and those who questioned.

The story of Yousuf warned the people of Makkah, as if to say – you are behaving with Muhammad (s.a.w.s) the same way the brothers of Yousuf behaved with him; therefore, you also expect to meet with the same end.

verses.text: Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the Book that makes things clear. (Surah Yousuf : Section 1)
Allah reveals to you (O Muhammad s.a.w.s), the best of stories through this Quran, though before this you were one of those who did not know. (Surah Yousuf : Section 1)
Yousuf (a.s) saw a dream wherein 11 stars, the sun and the moon prostrate before him. He conveyed this dream to his father Yaqoob (a.s). (Surah Yousuf : Section 1)
Yaqoob a.s said not to reveal the dream to his brothers, lest they plot an evil scheme against Yousuf. He further conveyed that it will happen as per the dream. (Surah Yousuf : Section 1)

There was much jealousy amongst the step brothers of Yousuf and they plotted to kill him. One of the elder brothers (by name Yahuda) opined not to kill Yousuf but to throw him into a well. (Surah Yousuf : Section 2)
The stepbrothers then persuaded their father to send Yousuf out to play with them, and that they will take good care of him. (Surah Yousuf : Section 2)
The brothers threw Yousuf into the well and brought a shirt stained with false blood to their father, claiming that a wolf ate Yousuf. (Surah Yousuf : Section 2)
His father cried: “No! Your souls have tempted you to evil. I need good patience! Allah alone can help me against that which you assert”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 2)
On the other side, a caravan passes by and rescues Yousuf from the well. They took him as a slave and sold him for a few dirhams. (Surah Yousuf : Section 2)
An Egyptian bought Yousuf and handed him to his wife asking her to be kind to him, and maybe they would adopt him as their son. (Surah Yousuf : Section 3)
When Yousuf reached maturity, Allah bestowed upon him wisdom and knowledge. (Surah Yousuf : Section 3)
The lady of the house (i.e his master’s wife) tried to seduce Yousuf. She bolted the door and said: “Come!” (Surah Yousuf : Section 3)
Yousuf replied: “May Allah protect me from this! My lord (his master) has provided me with good residence. Should I betray his trust? Surely, wrongdoers do not prosper”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 3)

She advanced towards him and Yousuf saw a sign from his Rabb, and thus Allah shielded him from indecency and immodesty. (In the Torah this sign is referred to an image of his father Yaqoob (a.s) appearing on the wall with his finger raised) (Surah Yousuf : Section 3)

The lady of the house and Yousuf rush towards the door. In order to stop him she catches his shirt, as a result of which the shirt gets ripped from behind. As they reach to the door they come face to face with her husband. (Surah Yousuf : Section 3)
The lady says that it was Yousuf who had intended evil against her, while Yousuf says that it was she, who tried to seduce him. (Surah Yousuf : Section 3)

The husband takes account of the situation and one member from the lady’s family opined that if his shirt is ripped from the front, then she is speaking the truth and he is lying. But if the shirt is ripped from behind, then he is speaking the truth and she is lying. (Surah Yousuf : Section 3)
The husband saw that the shirt was ripped from behind and he admonishes her and asks her to seek forgiveness for her sins. (Surah Yousuf : Section 3)
Rumors go around amongst the women of the city, that the lady of the house has gone mad over her young slave. (Surah Yousuf : Section 4)
The lady invites the women for a banquet and gives each of them a knife. (Surah Yousuf : Section 4)

(While they are reclining on couches) and are engaged in cutting foodstuff, she asks Yousuf to come out before them. The women at the table are so amazed at his beauty that they cut their own hands and say: “Good Lord! He is no human being; he is but a noble angel”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 4)

The lady then says: “Well, this is the one about whom you blamed me. No doubt I seduced him, but he refused. And if he refuses to obey my order, he will certainly be thrown into prison and be disgraced”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 4)

Yousuf (a.s) prays: “O my Rabb! Prison is more to my liking than to which they invite me; and unless You ward off their cunning scam from me, I may, feel inclined towards them and become one of the ignorants”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 4)
Allah answered his prayers and warded off the schemes of the women. (Surah Yousuf : Section 4)
But even after all the evidences they had seen (of his innocence and the guilt of their women), they thought it proper to send him to prison for a while. (Surah Yousuf : Section 4)
Two young men entered the prison along with Yousuf. They both have a dream and share their dream with Yousuf. They ask Yousuf to help interpret their dreams for them. (Surah Yousuf : Section 5)
The one who had birds eating bread from the top of his head - death was destined to him, Yousuf revealed. (Surah Yousuf : Section 5)
Another who was pressing wine - he would be released and would serve the king, Yousuf revealed. (Surah Yousuf : Section 5))

Yousuf called on to the young men in prison to worship one Allah. It is the grace of Allah that He has not made us servants of anyone else other than Himself, yet most people are not grateful. (Surah Yousuf : Section 5)
One day, the king of Egypt saw in his dream seven fat cows being eaten up by seven lean ones. Also seven green ears of corn and seven dried ones. (Surah Yousuf : Section 6)

The ministers could not interpret the dream. Thereupon one of the two inmates from the prison who was released, remembers Yousuf after all this time, and asks permission to meet with Yousuf in prison. (Surah Yousuf : Section 6)
Yousuf interprets the dream saying that the people will cultivate for 7 years. They should store the corn they reap, except for what may be sufficient for their food. (Surah Yousuf : Section 6)
This will be followed by 7 years of hardship which will eat away all that would be stored. (Surah Yousuf : Section 6)
After that period, will come a year of abundant rain in which the people would press (olives, grapes etc.). (Surah Yousuf : Section 6)
The king orders that Yousuf be brought to him. Yousuf refuses to come and asks that the king first investigate about the women who cut their hands. (Surah Yousuf : Section 7)

The women are questioned and the truth finally comes out; the lady of the house (whose name is popularly referred to as Zulaikha) admits that it was she who attempted to seduce Yousuf. (Surah Yousuf : Section 7)

Yousuf says that the reason he wanted the king to enquire, was so that the Egyptian master who bought him would remove any doubt on his mind that it was Yousuf who betrayed him. (Surah Yousuf : Section 7)
Allah does not let the scams of the treacherous to succeed. (Surah Yousuf : Section 7)
Yousuf says to the king, to place him over all the resources of the land, and the king grants him his request. (Surah Yousuf : Section 7)

Thus, Allah established Yousuf in the land to live therein anywhere he wished. Allah bestows His mercy on whom He pleases, and Allah does not let the reward of good people to be lost. (Surah Yousuf : Section 7)

Several years later, when the famine came and there was no food available outside of Egypt, Yousuf’s step brothers came to him for food against their trading stock. (Yousuf would give one camel load of grain for one family for one year against their trading stocks which would be in form of money or goods). Yousuf recognized them, but they did not recognize Yousuf. (Surah Yousuf : Section 8)
Yousuf told them to bring their half-brother (i.e Yousuf’s blood brother, Benjamin) to him next time and if not they would not get grain. (Surah Yousuf : Section 8)

Also, he asked his servants to put his brothers trading stock (the money which the brothers gave), back into the saddle bags so that they would know about it only when they reach their family, and they would surely come back. (Surah Yousuf : Section 8)

When Yousuf’s brothers returned to their father, they said: “Father! Grain is henceforth denied unless we take our step brother with us; please send our brother with us so that we may get our measure; we take full responsibility for his safety”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 8)

When they opened their baggage, they discovered that their trading stock was returned back to them and they could get more food easily. They cried with joy and pleaded with their father to send their step brother with them. (Surah Yousuf : Section 8)
Yaqoob (a.s) reluctantly agrees to send his son Benjamin with them, reminding them about what happened with Yousuf. (Surah Yousuf : Section 8)

He takes a pledge from them in Allah’s name, to bring Benjamin back and sends them off saying: “In Allah do I put my trust, and in Him let all those that trust, put their trust in Him” (Surah Yousuf : Section 8)

When the brothers arrived to Egypt, Yousuf called his brother Benjamin alone and said: “In fact, I am your brother (Yousuf), now you need not grieve at what they had been doing”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 9)
While Yousuf was arranging the loads for their provisions, he put the royal drinking cup into his brother (Benjamin)’s pack. (Surah Yousuf : Section 9)

Later on a crier called: “O people of the caravan! You must be thieves”. The royal servants said: “We have lost the King’s drinking cup. The one who brings it will be awarded a camel load of food”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 9)

The brothers plead that none of them have done such a thing. The royal servants ask what the punishment should be if they are liars. To this, the brothers say: “The punishment is: he in whose pack you find the royal cup will be made your bondsman”. Yousuf gets all his brothers’ bags to be checked. (Surah Yousuf : Section 9)
Yousuf first begins to search the pack of his stepbrothers before the pack of his own brother Benjamin. Finally, he took the kings drinking cup out of Benjamin’s pack. (Surah Yousuf : Section 9)

The stepbrothers plead to Yousuf saying: “O Aziz! He (i.e Benjamin) has a very aged father who may not be able to survive without him; so please take one of us instead of him. We see that you are one of those who do good to others”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 9)
Yousuf refuses to let go of Benjamin saying that it would be unjust to seize anyone else other than from whose bag they found the cup. (Surah Yousuf : Section 9)

The stepbrothers hold a private meeting, and the eldest brother reminds them of the pledge they have given to their father and how they fell short of their duty with respect to Yousuf. He says: “I am not going to leave this land until my father gives me permission or Allah decides for me”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 10)
He asks the others to go and tell their father, that Benjamin committed theft and was kept back. (Surah Yousuf : Section 10)

Upon hearing this news, Yaqoob (a.s) cries “No! Your souls have contrived a story for you”. He then says: “Well, I will bear this too with good patience. May be Allah will bring them all back to me. Indeed, He is the Knowledgeable, the Wise”.
He turned his face away from them and cried: “Alas for Yousuf!” His eyes became white with grief, and he became sorely oppressed. (Surah Yousuf : Section 10)
His sons turned to him saying: “By Allah! It appears that you will not cease to remember Yousuf until you ruin your health or kill yourself”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 10)
Yaqoob (a.s) said: “I complain of my distress and grief to Allah alone and I know from Allah what you do not know”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 10)
He urged his sons to go and search for Yousuf and his brother. Never give up hope of Allah’s mercy; in fact, none despair of Allah’s mercy except the unbelieving people. (Surah Yousuf : Section 10)

After some time passed, the brothers went back to Yousuf and said that their family is in great distress. They further pleaded that they have come with poor capital to buy food. They requested Yousuf to give them full quota and to treat it as charity. (Surah Yousuf : Section 10)
Hearing this, Yousuf could not contain himself anymore and said: “Do you know what you did to Yousuf and his brother while acting out of ignorance?” (Surah Yousuf : Section 10)

This took the brothers by surprise and they questioned whether he was really Yousuf. To this he replied: “Yes! I am Yousuf. Verily, he who fears Allah and is patient, then indeed, Allah does not let the reward of the good-doers be wasted”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 10)
Yousuf further said: “There is no blame on you today. May Allah forgive you! He is the most Merciful of those who show mercy!” (Surah Yousuf : Section 10)
Yousuf then asks his brothers to go and cast his shirt over his father’s face and to come back with all the members of the family. (Surah Yousuf : Section 10)

When the brothers started from Egypt, Yaqoob (a.s) could smell the scent of Yousuf (although he was in Canaan or near Jordan). He said: “Certainly I feel the scent of Yousuf, even though you may think I am out of my mind”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 11)
The brothers reached their father and cast Yousuf’s shirt on his face and he regained sight. (Surah Yousuf : Section 11)
The brothers pleaded for forgiveness and Yaqoob (a.s) said: “Soon I would ask forgiveness for you from my Rabb; surely He is the one Who is the Forgiving, the Merciful”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 11)
When they came to Egypt, Yousuf took his parents to himself and raised them to his throne and they all fell down in prostration before him. (Surah Yousuf : Section 11)
Yousuf said to his father: “O my father! This is the interpretation of my old dream. My Rabb has really made it come true”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 11)

Yousuf continued: “It was Allah’s grace that He took me out of prison and brought you all here from bedouin life, after Shaitaan had stirred up strife between me and my brothers. Surely, my Rabb is gracious to whom He wills. Surely, He is the One Who is the Knowledgeable, the Wise!”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 11)

Yousuf (a.s) then made a dua: “O, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and in the hereafter; make me die as a Muslim and admit me among the righteous”. (Surah Yousuf : Section 11)

This story (O Muhammad (s.a.w.s)), which We have revealed to you is a news of the unseen; for you were not there with the brothers of Yousuf when they conspired and put together their plan against him. (Surah Yousuf : Section 11)

This story is not an invented tale, but a confirmation of previous scriptures – a detailed exposition of all things, and is a guidance and blessing for the people who believe. (Surah Yousuf : Section 12)
